hadiths.english_translation: Narrated by Al-Qasim ibn Muhammad: Yazid ibn Abd al-Malik separated between men and their wives who were ummahat awlad (mothers of children) of men who had died, and they married them after one or two menstrual periods, so he separated between them until they observe waiting period of four months and ten days. Al-Qasim ibn Muhammad said: Glory be to Allah, Allah says in His Book: 'And those who die among you and leave wives behind' - they are not among the wives.

hadiths.arabicText: وَحَدَّثَنِي /12 مَالِك /12 ، عَنْ /94 يَحْيَى بْنِ سَعِيدٍ L8272 /94 ، /27 عَنِ /26 الْقَاسِمِ بْنِ مُحَمَّدٍ L1598 /26 ، أَنَّهُ كَانَ يَقُولُ : /20 " عِدَّةُ أُمِّ الْوَلَدِ إِذَا تُوُفِّيَ عَنْهَا سَيِّدُهَا حَيْضَةٌ " /27 . قَالَ /12 مَالِكٌ /12 : /10 وَهُوَ الْأَمْرُ عِنْدَنَا /10 . قَالَ /12 مَالِكٌ /12 : /10 وَإِنْ لَمْ تَكُنْ مِمَّنْ تَحِيضُ ، فَعِدَّتُهَا ثَلَاثَةُ أَشْهُرٍ /10

hadiths.english_translation: It reached Malik that Sa'id ibn al-Musayyab and Sulayman ibn Yasar used to say: The waiting period of a female slave when her husband dies is two months and five nights. And it was narrated to me from Malik, from Ibn Shihab, similar to that. Malik said regarding a male slave who divorces a female slave with a divorce that is not final and he has the right to take her back, then he dies while she is in her waiting period from his divorce: She observes the waiting period of a female slave whose husband has died - two months and five nights. And if she is freed and he has the right to take her back, then she does not choose separation from him after being freed until he dies while she is in her waiting period from his divorce, she observes the waiting period of a free woman whose husband has died - four months and ten days. That is because the waiting period of death fell upon her after she was freed, so her waiting period is the waiting period of a free woman. Malik said: This is the matter among us.

hadiths.arabicText: حَدَّثَنِي /22 يَحْيَى /22 ، عَنْ /12 مَالِك /12 ، أَنَّهُ بَلَغَهُ ، /27 أَنَّ /26 سَعِيدَ بْنَ الْمُسَيَّبِ L3299 /26 ، /26 وَسُلَيْمَانَ بْنَ يَسَارٍ L3634 /26 ، كَانَا يَقُولَانِ : /20 " عِدَّةُ الْأَمَةِ إِذَا هَلَكَ عَنْهَا زَوْجُهَا شَهْرَانِ وَخَمْسُ لَيَالٍ " /27 . وَحَدَّثَنِي ، عَنْ /12 مَالِكٍ /12 ، عَنِ /94 ابْنِ شِهَابٍ L7272 /94 ، مِثْلَ ذَلِكَ

hadiths.english_translation: Narrated by Abu Sa'id al-Khudri: We went out with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ in the expedition of Banu al-Mustaliq, and we captured some female captives from the Arab captives. We desired women, and celibacy became hard upon us, and we loved the ransom. So we wanted to practice withdrawal (coitus interruptus), and we said: Shall we practice withdrawal while the Messenger of Allah ﷺ is among us before we ask him? So we asked him about that, and he said: 'It does not matter if you do not do it, for there is no soul that is to be created until the Day of Resurrection except that it will be created.' And it was narrated to me from Malik, from Abu al-Nadr, the freed slave of Umar ibn Ubaydullah, from Amir ibn Sa'd ibn Abi Waqqas, from his father, that he used to practice withdrawal. And it was narrated to me from Malik, from Abu al-Nadr, the freed slave of Umar ibn Ubaydullah, from Ibn Aflah, the freed slave of Abu Ayyub al-Ansari, from an umm walad of Abu Ayyub al-Ansari, that he used to practice withdrawal. And it was narrated to me from Malik, from Nafi', from Abdullah ibn Umar, that he did not practice withdrawal and he disliked withdrawal.

hadiths.arabicText: حَدَّثَنِي /22 يَحْيَى /22 ، عَنْ /12 مَالِك /12 ، عَنْ /94 رَبِيعَةَ بْنِ أَبِي عَبْدِ الرَّحْمَنِ L2885 /94 ، عَنْ /26 مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ يَحْيَى بْنِ حَبَّانَ L7319 /26 ، عَنِ /26 ابْنِ مُحَيْرِيزٍ L5071 /26 ، أَنَّهُ قَالَ : دَخَلْتُ الْمَسْجِدَ ، فَرَأَيْتُ أَبَا سَعِيدٍ الْخُدْرِيَّ ، فَجَلَسْتُ إِلَيْهِ ، فَسَأَلْتُهُ عَنِ الْعَزْلِ ، /27 فَقَالَ /93 أَبُو سَعِيدٍ الْخُدْرِيُّ L3260 /93 : خَرَجْنَا مَعَ رَسُولِ اللَّهِ صَلَّى اللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ فِي غَزْوَةِ بَنِي الْمُصْطَلِقِ ، فَأَصَبْنَا سَبْيًا مِنْ سَبْيِ الْعَرَبِ ، فَاشْتَهَيْنَا النِّسَاءَ ، وَاشْتَدَّتْ عَلَيْنَا الْعُزْبَةُ وَأَحْبَبْنَا الْفِدَاءَ ، فَأَرَدْنَا أَنْ نَعْزِلَ ، فَقُلْنَا : نَعْزِلُ ، وَرَسُولُ اللَّهِ صَلَّى اللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ بَيْنَ أَظْهُرِنَا قَبْلَ أَنْ نَسْأَلَهُ ، فَسَأَلْنَاهُ عَنْ ذَلِكَ ، فَقَالَ : /20 " مَا عَلَيْكُمْ أَنْ لَا تَفْعَلُوا ، مَا مِنْ نَسَمَةٍ كَائِنَةٍ إِلَى يَوْمِ الْقِيَامَةِ إِلَّا وَهِيَ كَائِنَةٌ " /27

hadiths.english_translation: Narrated by Zayd ibn Thabit: Al-Hajjaj ibn Amr ibn Ghaziyyah said that he was sitting with Zayd ibn Thabit when Ibn Qahd, a man from the people of Yemen, came to him and said: O Abu Sa'id, I have slave girls for whom my wives who I keep are not more pleasing to me than them, but not all of them please me to bear children from me. Shall I practice withdrawal? Zayd ibn Thabit said: Give him a fatwa, O Hajjaj. He said: I said: May Allah forgive you, we only sit with you to learn from you. He said: Give him a fatwa. He said: So I said: 'It is your tillage, if you wish you water it, and if you wish you leave it thirsty.' He said: And I used to hear that from Zayd, so Zayd said: He spoke the truth.

hadiths.arabicText: وَحَدَّثَنِي ، عَنْ /12 مَالِك /12 ، عَنْ /94 ضَمْرَةَ بْنِ سَعِيدٍ الْمَازِنِيِّ L3980 /94 ، /27 عَنِ /26 الْحَجَّاجِ بْنِ عَمْرِو بْنِ غَزِيَّةَ L2301 /26 أَنَّهُ كَانَ جَالِسًا عِنْدَ زَيْدِ بْنِ ثَابِتٍ ، فَجَاءَهُ ابْنُ قَهْدٍ رَجُلٌ مِنْ أَهْلِ /60 الْيَمَنِ /60 ، فَقَالَ : يَا أَبَا سَعِيدٍ ، إِنَّ عِنْدِي جَوَارِيَ لِي لَيْسَ نِسَائِي اللَّاتِي أُكِنُّ بِأَعْجَبَ إِلَيَّ مِنْهُنَّ ، وَلَيْسَ كُلُّهُنَّ يُعْجِبُنِي أَنْ تَحْمِلَ مِنِّي ، أَفَأَعْزِلُ ؟ فَقَالَ /93 زَيْدُ بْنُ ثَابِتٍ L3131 /93 : أَفْتِهِ يَا حَجَّاجُ

hadiths.english_translation: Narrated by Ibn Abbas: Ibn Abbas was asked about withdrawal, so he called a slave girl of his and said: 'Inform them,' but she was shy. He said: 'It is that - as for me, I do it,' meaning that he practices withdrawal. Malik said: A man should not practice withdrawal from a free woman except with her permission, and there is no harm in practicing withdrawal from his slave girl without her permission, and whoever has a slave girl belonging to other people under him, he should not practice withdrawal except with their permission.

hadiths.english_translation: Narrated by Umm Habibah: Zaynab bint Abi Salamah said: I entered upon Umm Habibah, the wife of the Prophet ﷺ, when her father Abu Sufyan ibn Harb died. Umm Habibah called for perfume that had yellowness in it - khaluq or something else - and she applied it to a slave girl, then wiped her cheeks with it. Then she said: By Allah, I have no need for perfume, except that I heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ say: 'It is not lawful for a woman who believes in Allah and the Last Day to mourn for a deceased person for more than three nights, except for a husband - four months and ten days.'

hadiths.english_translation: Narrated by Umm Salamah: Zaynab said: And I heard my mother Umm Salamah, the wife of the Prophet ﷺ, say: A woman came to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and said: O Messenger of Allah, my daughter's husband died, and her eyes are troubling her, should she apply kohl to them? The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: 'No,' twice or three times, each time saying: No. Then he said: 'It is only four months and ten days. And one of you in the Days of Ignorance used to throw a piece of dung at the completion of a year.' Humayd ibn Nafi' said: I said to Zaynab: What is throwing a piece of dung at the completion of a year? Zaynab said: 'When a woman's husband died, she would enter a small hut, wear the worst of her clothes, and not touch perfume or anything, until a year passed. Then she would be brought an animal - a donkey, a sheep, or a bird - and she would break her mourning with it. Rarely would she break her mourning with anything except that it died. Then she would come out and be given a piece of dung to throw, then she would return to whatever she wished of perfume or other things.' Malik said: Al-hifsh is a low-quality house, and 'taftaddu' means she rubs her skin with it like a charm.
